answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable crystal bond before it can earn fees; a Sybil attacker must fund each extra identity separately, so splitting one reputation across a thousand accounts ties up a thousand bonds and incurs the opportunity cost of locked capital. Validators can set the bond high enough to exceed the expected gain from cheap impersonation, while a velvet queue delays withdrawals and a beacon-linked penalty slashes a proven attacker's bond, making coordinated fake identities expensive rather than free.
